title: Where the Pier 45 fire insurance money went

beats.text: A warehouse burned on Pier 45. The Port and the fishers owned different property.

visual.sub: One fire produced claims from two different sets of owners

beats.text: The Port first received $6.1 million from its own property insurance.

visual.label: One fire produced claims from two different sets of owners

beats.text: The next fiscal year brought another $18.856 million.

visual.label: The public ledger identifies the demolition contractor and a subcontractor reconciliation

beats.text: Six City vouchers match the demolition contractor’s payment exactly.

visual.kicker: The public ledger identifies the demolition contractor and a subcontractor reconciliation

beats.text: The fishermen’s separate settlement totaled $6.2 million.

visual.label: The fishing group settled for $6.2 million with three contributions

beats.text: Liability insurers and two security firms split that obligation.
The Port identified a deductible of up to $100,000.

visual.kicker: The fishing group settled for $6.2 million with three contributions

beats.text: Its property insurers also gave up recovery claims against the security contractors.
Years later, the Port appropriated $75.4 million from the property proceeds.

visual.label: The capital budget directed part of the property-insurance proceeds beyond the damaged shed

beats.text: It allocated $35.4 million to repair the west apron.

visual.label: The capital budget directed part of the property-insurance proceeds beyond the damaged shed

beats.text: Another $40 million went to the broader wharf program.

visual.label: The capital budget directed part of the property-insurance proceeds beyond the damaged shed

beats.text: The Port listed an $11.2 million request. Its first application was unsuccessful.

visual.kicker: The apron repair also sought federal aid

beats.text: Project invoices would show how much was actually spent.
